instruction: The mouse pointer is moving too fast for me to control accurately. Could you slow down the mouse speed to make it easier to use?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: MOUSE_SPEED=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.mouse speed 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$MOUSE_SPEED" ]; then SPEED_VALUE=$(echo "$MOUSE_SPEED" | grep -oE '[-0-9.]+'); if [ -n "$SPEED_VALUE" ] && [ "$(echo "$SPEED_VALUE < 0" | bc -l 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" = "1" ]; then echo "Mouse speed reduced (speed: $SPEED_VALUE)"; else echo "Mouse speed not reduced (speed: $SPEED_VALUE)"; fi; else echo "Could not read mouse speed"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires reducing mouse speed for better control. Evaluator checks if mouse speed is negative (slower than default 0.0) using gsettings. Similar difficulty to original task - both are single accessibility/usability settings. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary score: 1.0 if mouse speed < 0, 0.0 otherwise
